questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: Which signal best represents a consumer-facing pipeline outcome?
options: Every worker in the pool reports a healthy state to the monitoring agent
The job's run state has stayed RUNNING for the whole scheduled window
The curated table is complete and published by the time it was promised
The pipeline's retry count stayed below the threshold set for the stage

questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: What does Cloud Logging provide?
options: Centralized structured logs that can be searched, routed, and made into metrics
Time-series metrics with dashboards and the alerting policies that read them
The job graph and per-step detail for a running distributed pipeline
A record of every principal that has been granted a role on a resource

questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: Why include one run ID across orchestration and processing logs?
options: So the log router can decide which sink each individual entry belongs in
So log-based metrics can count the entries a single stage has emitted
So audit logs can attribute each write to the identity that performed it
So one execution can be traced from trigger to published dataset

questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: What makes an alert actionable?
options: It fires on each transient retry, so nothing is ever missed by responders
It names the impact, the current value, an owner, and the runbook to follow
It routes every severity to the same channel, so triage stays consistent
It repeats until acknowledged, which guarantees somebody eventually acts

questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: A streaming job is RUNNING but consumers see data two hours late. Which metric deserves immediate attention?
options: System lag and data freshness on the job's streaming stages
The count of log entries the job has written in the last two hours
The number of retries the orchestrator recorded for this run's trigger
The billing export's cost per completed job over the same window

questions.topic: Monitoring and Logging Data Pipelines on GCP
questions.question: A quality rule finds materially incomplete output. What should the publication path do?
options: Publish it and record the rule failure as a time series for later review
Publish it, since a rule failure is advisory until an operator confirms it
Publish a partial table and let each consumer filter the missing partitions
Withhold or quarantine the unsafe output and alert its accountable owner

questions.question: Which response commonly indicates rate limiting?
options: HTTP 201
HTTP 302
HTTP 429
HTTP 101

questions.question: What does a Google Cloud budget normally do?
options: It caps spend at the configured amount and blocks further service use
It tracks spend against a threshold and sends the notifications set on it
It raises the project's quotas automatically once spend crosses the limit
It deletes the resources whose SKU accounts for most of the month's cost

questions.question: How should a client respond to a retryable rate quota error?
options: Back off exponentially with jitter, and bound the number of attempts
Retry immediately in a tight loop until the quota window resets itself
Create additional projects so the load spreads across separate quotas
Raise the request's priority so the service admits it ahead of others

questions.question: Which analysis best explains a cost increase?
options: Compare only the month's total against the previous month's total bill
Assume the growth is fraud until the billing account has been audited
Look at the newest deployment, since cost changes always follow releases
Separate workload volume, unit price, and efficiency, then attribute by SKU

questions.question: A deterministic invalid schema fails every run. What is the correct response?
options: Retry with a longer backoff, since the failure will eventually clear itself
Stop retrying, correct or quarantine the incompatibility, then rerun it
Request a quota increase on the service that reported the failed job
Route the whole stream to the dead-letter path and leave it there

questions.question: An API reports no quota project set. Which configuration should be checked first?
options: The KMS key ring's rotation period on the project holding the resource
The partition filter requirement on the table the request is reading
The consumer or billing project the request accounts its quota against
The organization policy that constrains where the resource may live

questions.question: What is an ephemeral Dataproc cluster?
options: A cluster whose workers are all Spot capacity that can vanish at any time
A cluster kept warm between jobs so interactive users avoid startup time
A cluster whose image and configuration are patched in place on each run
A cluster created for one workflow and deleted once it finishes

questions.question: Which workload often favors a persistent cluster?
options: A steady stream of short interactive jobs that cannot absorb startup time
A monthly batch run whose schedule leaves plenty of room for provisioning
A one-off migration that needs its own image version and network settings
A pipeline whose only durable state already lives in Cloud Storage tables

questions.question: What is a key advantage of ephemeral clusters?
options: They remove the startup delay that a provisioning step would otherwise add
They give per-workload sizing and isolation while cutting idle compute cost
They make the workers' local disks durable across the cluster's deletion
They let several teams share one identity, which simplifies the IAM model

questions.question: Where should durable inputs and outputs of an ephemeral Spark job live?
options: On the worker nodes' local disks, which the job checkpoints between stages
In the driver's memory, so the executors read them without a network hop
In Cloud Storage, BigQuery, or a suitable external metastore
In the cluster's own logs, which the workflow reads back on the next run

questions.question: How can a team upgrade a busy persistent cluster with lower disruption?
options: Build a new versioned cluster, route new jobs to it, then drain the old one
Patch each running executor in place and restart the driver afterwards
Delete the cluster at once and recreate it from the same saved template
Attach secondary workers on the new image so both versions run together

questions.question: When is Spot or preemptible worker capacity most appropriate?
options: For the cluster's control components, which restart quickly after loss
For a job whose tasks cannot be retried once they have been scheduled
For holding the only copy of an intermediate result between two stages
For fault-tolerant work that has been tested against worker loss

questions.question: What does RPO measure?
options: The target time within which service must be restored after a failure
The maximum acceptable data loss, expressed as an interval of time
The interval at which a replica's lag is sampled and reported
The retention period a backup must be kept for before deletion

questions.question: What does RTO measure?
options: The number of current replicas a service is required to maintain
The maximum data loss the business is willing to accept in time
The target elapsed time to bring the service back into operation
The interval between two consecutive backups of the same dataset

questions.question: Why is replication not a substitute for backup?
options: Replicas are stored in the same region, so one outage removes them all
Replication runs on a schedule, so its copies are always hours behind
Replicas hold no schema, so a restore cannot rebuild the original table
Replication faithfully copies a deletion or corruption out to every replica

questions.question: What does a restore exercise prove that a backup-success event does not?
options: That the data and its dependencies can be recovered and then validated
That the backup's bytes were written to their destination without any error
That the replication lag on the secondary stayed inside its objective
That the retention policy on the backup vault has not yet expired

questions.question: A workload requires a very short RTO. Which design implication is most likely?
options: Backups must be taken more often so the recovery point moves closer
Warm recovery capacity and automated failover steps become necessary
The secondary region can be provisioned only after the incident starts
Restore instructions can live inside the component being recovered

questions.question: What must be controlled after a failover that accepts writes?
options: The retention window on the primary's backups during the outage
The naming convention applied to resources in the recovery region
Split brain, how writes return, and reconciling the divergent records
The rotation schedule of the KMS key protecting the secondary copy

questions.question: What should determine the major products in a reference architecture?
options: The set of services the team has already studied for the certification
The breadth of the diagram, so each layer shows a recognizable product
The newest managed offering in each category the platform provides
The workload's requirements and the tradeoff each choice accepts

questions.question: Which flow order is most useful for a data architecture diagram?
options: Producers, ingestion, storage, processing, serving, then consumers
Identity, keys, catalog, monitoring, then the data path underneath
Consumers, then every administrator who can reach the same resources
Billing labels, project names, then the regions each service sits in

questions.question: Why label project, region, and trust boundaries?
options: They make each arrow read as an API call rather than a dependency
They surface the governance, location, and ownership decisions made
They guarantee that every service drawn inside them is multi-regional
They remove the need to show identities at the important transitions

questions.question: Which element should be drawn separately from the primary data flow?
options: The identity each service uses when it writes to its own destination
The dead-letter destination that catches the records a stage rejects
The backup and replication paths, each annotated with its RPO and RTO
The quality gate that decides whether a curated table gets published

questions.question: What is the best way to validate an architecture diagram?
options: Confirm that every managed service on it has a named owning team
Confirm that each product's official icon and label are up to date
Confirm that no failure path clutters the main producer-to-consumer line of flow
Ask what happens on duplicates, schema change, outage, and quota exhaustion

questions.question: Which certification answer is strongest?
options: One tying a requirement to a configured product and its consequence
One that names the managed product for each layer of the architecture
One that lists the alternatives considered before the final selection
One that states the chosen design carries no meaningful disadvantage
